zh: 来电了！大概十分钟前恢复的。
en: The power's back {on}! It came back about ten minutes ago.
note: On means working or switched on. "The power's back on" means the electricity is working again.

zh: 都这么晚了，办公室的灯还亮着。
en: It's really late, but the lights are still {on} in the office.
note: On means switched on. Lights, the TV or the heater can be on or off.

zh: 周六的派对还照常办吗？
en: Is the party still {on} for Saturday?
note: For events, on means it is still happening as planned.

zh: 今晚八点有比赛直播，早点过来看。
en: The game's {on} at eight tonight, so come over early.
note: On means being shown on TV or happening at that time.

zh: 这周末电影院在放什么电影？
en: What's {on|showing|playing} at the movies this weekend?
note: "What's on" means what is being shown or what is happening, at the cinema, on TV or in town.

zh: 这笔交易黄了，他们最后一刻退出了。
en: The deal's {off}. They pulled out at the last minute.
note: Off means cancelled. If a deal or a plan is off, it is not going to happen.

zh: 牛奶好像坏了，闻起来怪怪的。
en: I think the milk's gone {off|bad|sour}. It smells funny.
note: For food, "gone off" means it has gone bad and you should not eat or drink it.

zh: 明天的会取消了，莎拉病了。
en: Tomorrow's meeting is {off|cancelled|canceled}. Sarah's sick.
note: Off means cancelled. "The meeting's off" is a very common, casual way to say it.

zh: 好了，我走了，明天见！
en: Right, I'm {off|going|leaving|heading off}. See you tomorrow!
note: "I'm off" means I am leaving now. It is a common way to say goodbye.

zh: 我明天休息，可以帮你搬家。
en: I'm {off|free} tomorrow, so I can help you move.
note: "I'm off tomorrow" means I am not working tomorrow. It is a day off.

zh: 暖气开了一整天，难怪这么热。
en: The heater's been {on} all day. No wonder it's so warm.
note: On means switched on and running, so the heater has been working all day.

zh: 在烧水吗？我好想喝杯茶。
en: Is the kettle {on}? I'd love a cuppa.
note: "Is the kettle on?" means is someone boiling water for tea or coffee.

zh: “我打赌你三十分钟跑不完五公里。”“赌就赌！”
en: 'I bet you can't run 5K in under thirty minutes.' 'You're {on}!'
note: "You're on!" means I accept your challenge or bet.

zh: 把钱包收起来，午饭我请。
en: Put your wallet away. Lunch is {on} me.
note: "It's on me" means I will pay for it.

zh: 能把音乐关小点吗？我在打电话。
en: Can you turn the music {down}? I'm on a call.
note: Turn down means make it quieter or lower. Turn up means louder or higher.

zh: 开大声点！我超喜欢这首歌。
en: Turn it {up}! I love this song.
note: Turn it up means make it louder. Turn it down means make it quieter.

zh: 抱歉，音乐会的票都卖完了。
en: Sorry, the concert tickets are sold {out}.
note: Sold out means there are none left to buy.

zh: 昨晚暴风雨过后就一直停电。
en: The power's been {out|off} since the storm last night.
note: "The power's out" means there is no electricity, usually because of a storm or a fault.

zh: 好消息，那款跑鞋又有货了。
en: Good news. Those running shoes are {back} in stock.
note: "Back in stock" means the shop has the item again after it ran out.

zh: 洪水过后，一切终于恢复正常了。
en: Things are finally {back} to normal after the floods.
note: "Back to normal" means things are the same as before the problem.

zh: 我的闹钟早上五点就响了。
en: My alarm went {off} at five this morning.
note: When an alarm goes off, it starts ringing. Here off does not mean stopped.

zh: 快吃吧，还有很多呢。
en: Eat {up}! There's plenty more.
note: "Eat up" means eat all your food, or go ahead and eat. Up often means completely.

zh: 大家把酒喝完吧，酒吧要关门了。
en: Drink {up}, guys. They're closing the bar.
note: "Drink up" means finish your drink. Up here means completely.

zh: 牛奶都用完了，我回家路上买一些。
en: We've used {up} all the milk, so I'll grab some on the way home.
note: "Use up" means use all of something until none is left.

zh: 烧烤还办吗？还是因为下雨取消了？
en: Is the barbecue still {on}, or has it been rained {off|out}?
note: On means still happening. "Rained off" means cancelled because of rain.

zh: 快点，不然赶不上公交了。
en: Hurry {up}, or we'll miss the bus.
note: "Hurry up" means go faster or be quicker. People say it all the time.

zh: 先让发动机冷却一下再检查机油。
en: Let the engine cool {down|off} before you check the oil.
note: "Cool down" means become cooler. Down shows something becoming less.

zh: 进屋前先擦干，你浑身在滴水。
en: Dry {off} before you come inside. You're dripping.
note: "Dry off" means make your body dry, for example with a towel after swimming.

zh: 我给你打电话，但你关机了。
en: I tried to call you, but your phone was {off}.
note: Off means switched off, so the phone was not on and could not ring.

zh: 公司的咖啡又没了。
en: We've run {out} of coffee at work again.
note: "Run out of" something means there is none left.

zh: 现在退潮了，我们可以走到那个小岛上去。
en: The tide's {out}, so we can walk across to the island.
note: "The tide's out" means the sea is low. When the tide is in, the water is high.

zh: 衣服还晾在外面，下雨前你能收进来吗？
en: The washing's still {out}. Can you bring it in before it rains?
note: "The washing's out" means the clothes are outside on the line drying.

zh: 给我留着门口的灯，我会晚点回来。
en: Leave the porch light {on} for me. I'll be home late.
note: "Leave something on" means do not switch it off.

zh: 牛奶喝完了，所以我喝了黑咖啡。
en: We'd {run out} of milk, so I had my coffee black.
note: "Run out of" means have none left. Out shows that something is finished.

zh: 我手机没话费了，得充值。
en: I need to {top up|recharge} my phone. I've got no credit left.
note: "Top up" means add more money to your phone or travel card, or fill something to the top.

zh: 我上班路上得加油了，油快没了。
en: I need to {fill up|top up|refuel|get petrol|gas up} on the way to work. I'm nearly out of petrol.
note: "Fill up" means fill the car's tank with petrol. Up means full.

zh: 比赛前一定要热身。
en: Make sure you {warm up} before the game.
note: "Warm up" means do light exercise to get your body ready.

zh: 先冷静一下，告诉我发生了什么。
en: Just {calm down|settle down|chill out|relax} and tell me what happened.
note: "Calm down" means become less upset or excited. Down often means less.

zh: 孩子们吃完晚饭终于安静下来了。
en: The kids finally {settled down|calmed down|quietened down|quieted down} after dinner.
note: "Settle down" means become calm and quiet after being excited or noisy.

zh: 下周一起喝杯咖啡聊聊近况吧。
en: Let's {catch up|meet up|get together} over coffee next week.
note: "Catch up" means meet a friend and talk about what has happened since you last met.

zh: 我修打印机修到放弃了，直接找了IT。
en: I {gave up|stopped} trying to fix the printer and called IT.
note: "Give up" means stop trying because it is too hard.

zh: 开心点！又不是世界末日。
en: {Cheer up}! It's not the end of the world.
note: "Cheer up" means try to feel happier. Up often means a better mood.

zh: 客人来之前你能帮我收拾一下吗？
en: Can you help me {tidy up|clean up|tidy|clean} before the guests arrive?
note: "Tidy up" means put things back in their place so the room looks neat.

zh: 我们周日上午都在收拾派对后的残局。
en: We spent Sunday morning {cleaning up|tidying up} after the party.
note: "Clean up" means make a place clean again after a mess.

zh: 你洗碗的话，我就做饭。
en: I'll cook if you {wash up|do the dishes|do the washing up|do the washing-up}.
note: In New Zealand and the UK, "wash up" means wash the dishes. In the US it means wash your hands.

zh: 票十分钟就卖光了。
en: The tickets {sold out|went} in ten minutes.
note: "Sell out" means all of them were sold, so none are left.

zh: 电已经恢复了，我终于可以给笔记本充电了。
en: The power has {come back on|come on}, so I can finally charge my laptop.
note: "Come back on" means start working again after it was off.

zh: 把暖气调小点，这里热死了。
en: {Turn down} the heater. It's boiling in here.
note: "Turn down" means make it lower or weaker, like the heat or the volume.

zh: 我还在厕所里，有人把灯关了。
en: Someone {turned off|switched off|turned out} the lights while I was still in the toilet.
note: "Turn off" means stop something working with a switch.

zh: 我们取消烧烤吧，要下大雨了。
en: Let's {call off|cancel} the barbecue. It's going to pour.
note: "Call off" means cancel an event. Off often means cancelled or stopped.

zh: 这家面包店的派不到十点就卖光了。
en: This bakery {sells out|runs out} of pies by ten.
note: "Sell out of" something means sell all of it, so there is none left.

zh: 你得放慢节奏，你太拼了。
en: You need to {slow down|ease up|ease off|take it easy}. You're working too hard.
note: "Slow down" means go slower, or do less and relax a bit.

zh: 重组之后，公司的情况慢慢稳定下来了。
en: Things are {settling down|calming down|quietening down|quieting down} at work after the restructure.
note: "Settle down" means become calm and normal again after a busy or difficult time.

zh: 你能把音量调大一点吗？我听不清。
en: Could you {turn up} the volume a bit? I can't hear.
note: "Turn up" means make it louder or higher.

zh: 圣诞节前我们把年假全用完了。
en: We {used up} all our annual leave before Christmas.
note: "Use up" means use all of something until none is left.

zh: 发生塌方后，那条路被封了好几个小时。
en: The road was {closed off|closed|blocked off|cordoned off|shut} for hours after the slip.
note: "Closed off" means blocked so nobody can go in. In New Zealand a slip is a landslide.

zh: 我用微波炉把剩菜热一下。
en: I'll {warm up|heat up} the leftovers in the microwave.
note: "Warm up" or "heat up" food means make it hot again.

zh: 你能烧壶水吗？
en: Can you {put|switch|turn} the kettle {on}?
note: "Put the kettle on" means start boiling water, usually to make tea.

zh: 没什么客人，他们就早早关店了。
en: Nobody was coming in, so they {closed up|shut up|closed|shut} the shop early.
note: "Close up" means close a shop or building for the day, locking everything.

zh: 音乐会已经取消了，不过之后的聚会照常举行。
en: The concert's been {called off|cancelled|canceled}, but the after-party is still {on}.
note: "Called off" means cancelled, and "still on" means still happening. On and off are opposites for plans.
